subject: Next steps & POC sprint charter — Helios Analytics
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@helios.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed POC sprint charter (Helios)

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth heading into the kickoff. Please confirm owners and any missing constraints.

Key pain points we heard (from your team):
- Embeddings latency spikes during batch inference causing downstream search timeouts (~P99).
- Per-query cost for large re-ranks is ballooning as query volume grows.
- Integration friction: existing infra is multi-cloud and you need VPC-friendly options + clear security controls.

Goals for the 6-week POC:
1) Reduce median embed+search latency and stabilize P95/P99 below targets (P95 < 120ms, P99 < 320ms) for typical queries.
2) Demonstrate >=35% reduction in per-token cost through batching/caching and model selection for your workload.
3) Produce an evaluation suite (sample prompt set + reference metrics) to compare quality across candidate models.

Proposed scope & acceptance criteria (POC sprint charter):
- Week 0 (prep): access & connectivity (VPC peering, API creds, anonymized sample dataset).
- Week 1–2: baseline: replay traffic, capture latency distribution and token usage; run initial evals on 2 model variants.
- Week 3–4: optimization sprints: enable prefix/KV caching, tune batching, evaluate quantized variant if acceptable.
- Week 5: final stability run & cost vs quality tradeoff report.
- Week 6: handoff & playbook: operational runbook + next-step recommendations.

Success metrics we'll track: P50/P95/P99 latency, tokens per request, cost per 1k queries, relative eval quality (BLEU/semantic-similarity + manual spot-checks).

Owners (please confirm):
- Helios: Alyssa Chen (technical lead), Tom Rivera (procurement/compliance).
- Redwood: Michael Grant (AE, engagement lead), Vanessa Ortiz (Solutions Engineer, evals + infra), Karthik Iyer (Customer Success, onboarding & SLA ops).

Access & setup asks (items for your infra team):
- Create a service account and grant read access to a test S3 bucket with anonymized dataset; send service account key or set up temporary signed URLs.
- Network: either VPC peering or allowlist Redwood's egress IPs for the trial.
- Provide initial sample of search queries (CSV) and a small ground-truth set for evals.

Attachments included: POC_Charter_Helios_v1.pdf (charter + milestones), access-checklist_helios.xlsx (detailed access steps), helios_sample_prompts.jsonl (example prompt set).

Can you confirm owners and whether next-Tuesday (Nov 2) 10:00–11:00 PT works for the kickoff? If that's tight, propose two alternatives.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Michael Grant

Thanks Mike — this is a great summary and captures our priorities. Confirming the following from our side: 

- Owners: I will be the technical point of contact. Tom (cc'd) will manage procurement and compliance checks. I'll loop our platform lead if needed.
- Timeline: 6-week plan works in principle. We have a compliance window in Week 2 where we will need to complete an internal security questionnaire — can Redwood provide the SOC2 summary and a short architecture note for our InfoSec team ahead of the kickoff?
- Data residency: we need assurance that logs/eval samples won't be stored in EU regions; our production runs will be US-only. Please confirm how trial artifacts are handled.

One more ask: for the evaluation suite, can you include an initial suggested set of 50 prompts that reflect our typical long-tail queries? We reviewed the sample prompts and will add 20 more, but we want Redwood to seed the eval set.

On timing — Nov 2 at 10:00 PT works for me. I've added Tom and pilot+helios to the thread for additional scheduling/visibility.

Short coordination notes before kickoff:

- Eval prompt set: I'll take the first pass at seeding 50 prompts that cover short/long-tail, re-rank, and multi-turn clarifications. Will share a draft in the Drive folder by EOD Wed.
- Dataset: we need an anonymized sample with at least 5k queries and 500 labeled references for spot checks. Alyssa — can you flag which bucket link you'll share? If you prefer, we can accept a signed temporary URL so we don't store keys.
- Models to test: recommend baseline open LLM A (full precision), A-quant (4-bit), and B (smaller, cheaper). Karthik — can you confirm whether we should enable continuous batching on the first run or hold off until baseline is captured? My preference: baseline first, then turn on batching to measure delta.
- Security pack: I'll attach the SOC2 summary and network architecture note in the Drive folder. Michael — can you add the InfoSec doc to the access checklist?

I can pick up the orchestration of the stability run and produce the cost/quality delta report in Week 5.

Subject: Confirmed: Kickoff agenda + pre-kickoff checklist (Nov 2, 10:00 PT)

A quick update and finalized checklist for the kickoff on Nov 2 at 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent). Agenda attached in the charter PDF; highlights below.

Kickoff agenda (45–60 min)
- Intros & scope (10 min) — confirm owners and success criteria
- Baseline instrumentation (10 min) — how you'll share sample traffic, test creds, and VPC option
- Eval design (10 min) — prompt set, labeling approach, quality metrics
- Run plan & rollback/fallback policies (10 min)
- Admins & next steps (5 min) — timeline for Week 0 access completion

Pre-kickoff checklist (items to complete before Nov 2):
- Helios: share temporary access to anonymized sample dataset (signed URL or service account).
- Helios: confirm network approach (VPC peering vs allowlist).
- Helios: confirm InfoSec review window — Redwood will upload SOC2 summary + architecture note to shared Drive by EOD Wed.
- Redwood: provide initial 50-seed prompt set and upload to Drive.
- Procurement: Tom, if possible please share any standard MSA redlines now; we'll queue legal for a quick review.

Attachments referenced here are included in the Drive folder and the PDF in this thread. Per Alyssa's request: Redwood confirms trial artifacts (logs and eval outputs) will be stored in US-only buckets for this POC and will not be replicated to other regions; final retention policy will be discussed at handoff.

Thanks everyone — see you on Nov 2. If anything pops up, reply-all and we'll handle before kickoff.

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
